issues.claim: The article on pair programming on Martin Fowler's site names knowledge sharing and onboarding among the main benefits of pairing.
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt only shows strong-style pairing being called useful for knowledge transfer and as an onboarding tool. It does not show a list of the main benefits of pairing, so this broader claim cannot be confirmed from it. The same sentence appears in locales.ru.explanation.
issues.suggestedFix: Narrow the claim to what the excerpt supports: the article describes strong-style pairing as particularly useful for knowledge transfer and as an onboarding tool that favours learning by doing. Apply the same change in ru.

issues.claim: The Daily Scrum exists to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the plan in time, and one of the Scrum values is openness: the team and its stakeholders are open about the work and the challenges.
issues.problem: The Scrum Guide excerpt covers backlog sizing, the Sprint Backlog as a plan by and for the Developers, and the Sprint Goal. It does not show the Daily Scrum wording or the openness value, so those two claims cannot be confirmed from the excerpt. The sizing and Sprint plan claims are supported. The same applies in ru.
issues.suggestedFix: Either confirm the Daily Scrum and openness lines against the full Scrum Guide text, or drop them. The remaining Scrum references (the Developers who do the work do the sizing, and the Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers) are enough. Apply the same change in ru.

issues.claim: An hour of this at the start often saves days of searching alone.
issues.problem: This is an unsourced empirical assertion, and it appears to be presented as part of what the article says.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften it to 'A short session like this at the start can save a lot of solo searching', or mark it clearly as the author's own experience. Apply the same change in ru.

issues.problem: The Russian link title is left in English, while the Scrum Guide title in ru is given as plain 'Scrum Guide'. The titles are also inconsistent with the en block ('Scrum Guide' vs 'The Scrum Guide').
issues.suggestedFix: Use "О парном программировании (martinfowler.com)" and "Руководство по Scrum", or at least make the titles consistent between ru and en.

issues.claim: The OWASP Vulnerability Disclosure Cheat Sheet describes this model and advises first finding out how the project accepts such reports: a security policy, a `security.txt` file, a dedicated reporting address.
issues.problem: The excerpt is written for organizations receiving reports. It tells them to publish contact details (security.txt, a dedicated security contact, a security@ address) and to publish an advisory after the fix. It does not show advice to a reporter to look up the project's policy first. Attributing that advice to the sheet is not supported by the excerpt. The same applies in ru.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword to match the source: 'The OWASP cheat sheet describes how organizations should publish contact channels (a security contact, a dedicated address, `security.txt`) and publish an advisory once the issue is fixed; so a reporter should look for such a channel first.' Apply the same change in ru.

issues.claim: After the fix, the maintainers publish an advisory; through the GitHub Advisory Database it reaches NuGet, and other users of the package get a warning on restore.
issues.problem: No cited link supports this chain, and the generator notes admit it is unverified. NuGet Audit does exist (NuGet 6.8 / .NET 8 SDK), but the transitive coverage and the default settings are not covered by the sources. The same applies in ru.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a Microsoft Learn link on auditing NuGet packages (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/auditing-packages) and a matching linkTitle in both locales, or soften to: 'Once published, the advisory can reach consumers through vulnerability feeds, and tools such as NuGet Audit can warn about the affected versions.'

issues.problem: The URL now redirects to https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/report-and-fix-vulnerabilities/report-privately. The page still supports the claim, but the link is stale.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the URL with the redirect target.
